title: Hello fellow Steam Next Fest ruiners, how's the event going for you so far ?
author: Odd_Revolution7522
selftext:
So apparently we've ruined Steam Next Fest for indie devs and players alike with an avalanche of AI slop.

Looking at some of the capsules and games out there, I can't entirely blame the critics. There's definitely some terrible, low-effort slop floating around.

On my end, though, the first few hours have been pretty positive! My game, Pixel Metropolis, has gained 84 wishlists so far and just crossed the 500 wishlist milestone.

Median demo playtime is still around 42 minutes, with an average of 1 hour and 47 minutes. So I'm pretty happy with that!

Hopefully, that's enough to pass the quality bar over the next few days.

I know this perspective is probably going to get buried in the broader discourse, but I think we're ultimately competing under the same conditions as traditional developers. Sure, we can develop faster, but we also have to overcome the stigma of being lumped in with all the low-effort AI slop.

Personally, I don't think allowing players to filter out AI-made games would be fair. Games should ultimately be judged on their own merits, not just the tools used to create them.

And I suspect the next few months will see more and more genuinely good AI-made games showing up, making that distinction increasingly important.

Anyway, enough about me. How's Next Fest going for the rest of you?

comments.author: Affectionate_Ad_9393
comments.body: Good on you! Link your game would like to have a look.

comments.author: Cinicola
comments.body:
A lot of negativity and somewhat fair reasons.  
I understand the issues with 1-prompt opus games, but others have spent 6 months with AI as an accelerator, with approval for designs and art. Including a buttload of changes..

 For many like us, we have the ideas, artstyle and feel in our minds and AI is helping us making our dream come true.

I never thought I would be able to publish a game on Steam - but here we are. 300 wishlists in and only positive reviews.

Artists are mad and rightfully so. I would also be mad, if my customers chose AI over me - but it's reality and not something that is going to go away anytime soon. Quite the contrary.

replies.author: Odd_Revolution7522
replies.body:
Yes, what I love about AI is that it will more people with more diverse ideas to make games.

The traditional skillset required to publish a game used to heavily skew towards people who have a more logical / systemic mind. 

I feel like we are going to see many more creative games in the future that explore new paths.

replies.author: Odd_Revolution7522

No offense taken.

It is an artistic choice, the nostalgia for old Impression games and Sim City 4 is voluntary.

I do leverage new tech such as shaders and higher definition of assets. And you can rotate the camera along all four isometric directions.

Rimworld, Factorio, Dwarf Fortress have been hugely successful without going 3D.

To me, its no better than when i see those rushed games that all have that generic UI that Codex always builds.
